Application type: Public client
Redirect URI: https://portal.azure.com
4. On your application page, select API Permissions > Add permission > APIs my
organization uses >, type Microsoft Threat Protection, and select Microsoft Threat
Protection. Your app can now access Microsoft Defender XDR.

 Tip
Microsoft Threat Protection is a former name for Microsoft Defender XDR, and will
not appear in the original list. You need to start writing its name in the text box to
see it appear.

Choose Delegated permissions. Choose the relevant permissions for your scenario
(for example Incident.Read), and then select Add permissions.
5. Select Grant admin consent. Every time you add a permission, you must select Grant
admin consent for it to take effect.

７ Note
You need to select the relevant permissions for your scenario. Read all incidents is
just an example. To determine which permission you need, please look at the
Permissions section in the API you want to call.
For instance, to run advanced queries, select the 'Run advanced queries' permission;
to isolate a device, select the 'Isolate machine' permission.
6. Record your application ID and your tenant ID somewhere safe. They're listed under
Overview on your application page.
For more information on Microsoft Entra tokens, see the Microsoft Entra tutorial.
Use the MSAL.PS library to acquire access tokens with Delegated permissions. Run the
